title: Monthly Fee of $10! OpenCode Go, an Open-Source AI Coding Tool, Announces Break-Even

content_html:
On September 12, 2026, Dax Raad, co-founder of the AI coding tool OpenCode, announced that its low-cost subscription service OpenCode Go, which costs only $10 per month, has achieved break-even for two consecutive weeks. In the current industry context where most AI coding tools still face high burn rates or monetize through data sales, this development marks a significant breakthrough in the commercial sustainability of low-cost AI subscription models.

OpenCode Go aims to provide developers with a cost-effective open-source AI coding experience through relaxed rate limits and stable access. This paid plan includes several high-performance models, such as Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7Code, GPT5.6Luna, MiniMax M3, Qwen3.7Plus, GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek V4Flash, DeepSeek V4.1Flash, MiMo-V2.5, and Muse Spark1.3Contributor.

In addition, OpenCode continues to offer a free service layer that includes models such as Nemotron3Ultra, Muse Spark1.3, Muse Spark1.2, Nemotron3.5Lightning, MiMo-2.5, Big Pickle, and Ling3.0Flash Fin. Developers can seamlessly switch to continue their work once they exhaust the quota for a single model.

As market competition intensifies, early free AI tools, including Windsurf (now renamed Devin), have tightened their free quotas, and AI startups are generally facing pressure to transition from user expansion to financial stability. The break-even of OpenCode Go not only validates the feasibility of commercializing open-source large models but also provides an important reference for the generative AI industry in exploring healthy and sustainable revenue models.
